question: Can actual SDK EventLog reconstruct immutable raw messages/branches after writer exit, serialize competing writers, and distinguish duplicate/gap/corrupt history?
real_code: Editable openhands-sdk EventLog, MessageEvent, LocalFileStore, atomic_write_text and FileLock; real separate Python processes on ext4
fixtures: Fixed typed message objects only; no replacement storage/event implementation; no Agent.run/LLM/provider

cases.input: writer appends3 UUID messages (root1,child2,sibling3) then exits; fresh reader
cases.expected: all3 exact IDs/text retained; branch to3 returns1,3; raw history still includes2

cases.input: fresh process appends ID1 with changed text
cases.expected: ValueError and original content unchanged; this is duplicate rejection, not idempotent outcome replay

cases.input: 4 OS processes each append2 unique UUID events to same store
cases.expected: reopened count8 unique and exact set; no process errors

cases.input: copy pristine store then replace middle JSON with invalid text
cases.expected: observe explicit load error, never accept corrupt payload as valid message

cases.input: copy pristine store then remove middle event JSON; reopen
cases.expected: observe whether complete history is rejected or silently reduced. Reduced length is capability gap, not successful recovery.

oracle: Fixed expected UUID/text/branch set independent from candidate caches; new reader and independent raw JSON/files inspection
stop: Each subprocess45seconds; retain failure; no NFS/machinepowerloss or automation dispatch proof
scope: SDK local event persistence and branch projection; full Conversation state autosave/recovery/toolsideeffects not executed. Automation tracked separately.
